solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Meat balls so got from stale lamb?

definitions.text: Meat balls so got from stale lamb?

parts.words: Meat balls so got from stale lamb?
parts.note: the letters of 'meat balls' are exactly those of 'stale lamb' reshuffled, so the phrase is what you get by rearranging it

explanation.surface: A cook makes meatballs from lamb past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about leftovers in the kitchen; the real point is the letters, since MEATBALLS and STALELAMB share the same nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something produced by rearranging the letters of another phrase has been put through that letter-shuffling process, described with the past participle.

clue.text: Original light opera starts for composer

parts.note: an original idea is a novel one

indicators.note: the starts of the two words light and opera are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A new light opera begins its run, credited to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor, famous for songs and musicals of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a well-known Welsh songwriter and composer of stage musicals.

clue.text: Moves right in — inflicts stab wound

indicators.note: in tells us the right letter is placed inside the word for moves

parts.note: to move is to go, so moves gives goes

explanation.surface: An attacker steps in and stabs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull or rhino that pierces a victim with its horn does so by goring, a stabbing wound.

clue.text: Half of soldiers responsible for motor part

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters of the word for soldiers are used

parts.note: the army is a body of soldiers
a responsible person is mature, grown-up and sensible

explanation.surface: Half the troops are blamed for a broken engine component.
explanation.definitionFit: The armature is the rotating wound coil in an electric motor, a component of it.

clue.text: Hitler mood faded to become politically moderate

indicators.note: the words are said to change into something else, so the letters are rearranged into a new phrase

explanation.surface: A dictator's temper cools until he turns into a centrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faded' does double duty in the surface but here it is part of the fodder, while 'to become' signals the rearrangement of HITLERMOODFADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the political centre, avoiding extremes of left or right, is described with this idiom.

clue.text: Free to engage drive that elevates site machine

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating means reading the letters upward, so the result is turned around
engaging something means taking it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
to egg on is to drive or urge forward

explanation.surface: Instructions for a free drive that lifts a machine on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: An excavator used on a construction site to dig out earth is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Leader cancelled demo in Bow

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed from the word for a demo

parts.note: a demo, or demonstration, is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest in an East London district was called off when its leader withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London, which makes it look like the place the demo was held; it is really the definition, a curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curved shape, and an arch is a curved structure spanning an opening.

clue.text: Stream diverted by what blocks it here?

definitions.text: Stream diverted by what blocks it here?

indicators.note: a diverted stream is sent on a different course, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that blocks a river

explanation.surface: Asking where a river is rerouted by the barrier that stops it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Amsterdam takes its name from a dam on the river Amstel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is named after a dam built across the Amstel river, so the clue describes the city.

clue.text: Cleaner forced to go topless in absurd act

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: going topless loses the top, which in a down clue is the first letter of the word

parts.note: to be forced to do something is to be made to do it

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is compelled to strip off in a ridiculous performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a pretence so obvious it is absurd, a farcical act put on for show.

clue.text: Finished as bridge?

definitions.meaning: something finished is done, at an end
a bridge is something that goes across a gap, as in an overpass

explanation.definitionFit: A game that is finished is done, and a bridge spans across a river or road.

clue.text: Ridiculous vehicle running on LPG in large island

parts.note: a ridiculous idea is mad
LPG is liquefied petroleum gas, so a vehicle powered by it is a gas car

explanation.surface: A silly car converted to gas fuel on a big island.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar, off the east coast of Africa, is one of the largest islands in the world.

clue.text: Confine and suffer defeat in court

indicators.note: in shows that the word for suffering defeat is placed inside the letters for court

parts.note: to suffer defeat is to lose

explanation.surface: A defendant is locked up after losing the case before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To closet someone is to shut them away in a private room, keeping them confined.

clue.text: Loyal follower — chap from Belgium?

definitions.meaning: a feudal vassal sworn to serve a lord
a man from Liège, a city in eastern Belgium

explanation.surface: A devoted supporter turns out to be a Belgian fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a vassal bound to serve his lord was his sworn man, a faithful follower.

clue.text: Harmony and love in musical work

parts.note: to act in concert is to act in harmony, in agreement
love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Agreement and affection are found in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a composition for a solo instrument with orchestra, a substantial piece of music.

clue.text: Stock phrases individuals associated with eastern tongue

parts.note: cant is hackneyed, insincere stock talk
single individuals are ones

explanation.surface: Clichés used by people tied to a language of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and Cantonese is the Chinese language spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong.

clue.text: Grass blown backwards does for example

indicators.note: the wind blowing it backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass that grows by water

explanation.surface: Wind blows a stand of grass back, doing so for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe, a female deer, so the definition is a category given by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Does are female deer, so they are examples of the animal named by the answer.

clue.text: Shifting in narrow lane's Ken Turner

indicators.note: in says the shuffled name goes inside the word for the narrow lane

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane between buildings

indicators.note: shifting means the three letters of Ken move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ken Turner is spotted moving about in a narrow lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken Turner' reads as a man's full name, but Turner is the definition: a small L-shaped tool that turns hexagonal screws.
explanation.definitionFit: This hexagonal tool is used to turn bolts and screws with a hexagonal socket head.

clue.text: Corner unseen in country garden

indicators.note: something unseen is not there, so these letters are removed from the country

parts.note: Sweden is a Scandinavian country
SW, southwest, is a corner of a map or compass

explanation.surface: A hidden corner in a rural garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country garden' reads as one phrase, but 'country' gives SWEDEN and 'garden' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Thoroughly cook little fish found beneath ocean

indicators.note: in a down clue, the fish below means its letters come after the ocean's

parts.note: the deep is a poetic word for the ocean
fry are young, small fish

explanation.surface: Small fish found deep under the sea get cooked through.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food by immersing it fully in hot fat is a method of cooking it through.

clue.text: Line through targets where hydroplant destroyed

indicators.note: the line runs through, so its letter goes inside the first target

parts.note: a tee is a mark aimed at in quoits or curling
a mark is a target, as in hitting the mark

explanation.surface: A line drawn through the targets at the site of a sabotaged power station.
explanation.walkthrough: Telemark is the Norwegian region where Allied commandos sabotaged the Nazi heavy-water plant at Vemork in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norsk Hydro heavy-water plant at Vemork in this Norwegian county was sabotaged in 1943.

clue.text: Musical instrument on floor in Habitat

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another means it sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a reed is a simple wind instrument, or the vibrating part of one
a bed is the floor of a sea or river

explanation.surface: A musical instrument left lying on the floor in the Habitat furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Habitat is a British home-furnishing chain, hence the capital letter; here it just means a natural home.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of reeds in shallow water is the natural home of many birds and insects.

clue.text: Male beast and one female in mountainous plateau

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A male animal and a female up on a high plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming an elevated block of high ground.

clue.text: Article in French newspaper it refreshes

indicators.note: in places the article inside the name of the French paper

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading daily newspaper in France
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a French daily that perks readers up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold fizzy citrus soft drink is the classic thing to quench thirst and refresh.

clue.text: Dodger Luke finally to face Anakin Skywalker

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the name Luke

parts.note: Anakin Skywalker becomes Darth Vader in Star Wars

explanation.surface: Luke Skywalker at last faces his father in a Star Wars showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dodges escapes or avoids something, such as a tax dodger avoiding payment.

clue.text: Tool that cuts into metal for so long

indicators.note: into means the tool's word is placed inside the symbol for the metal

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a tool for cutting threads or stamping metal

explanation.surface: A cutting tool is pressed into metal for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell, French for 'to God', said when parting, like the casual goodbye phrase.

clue.text: Dessert wine that causes another little wobble

parts.note: afters is British slang for the pudding course
hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A pudding wine that makes diners a bit unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is informal British for dessert; HOCK is a Rhine white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: After an earthquake, smaller tremors follow, each a lesser shake of the ground.

clue.text: Missile key computer company holds

indicators.note: the company's letters hold the key inside them

parts.note: IBM is the American computer company
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A computer firm keeps the key to a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercontinental ballistic missile is a long-range nuclear weapon, known by its initials.

clue.text: Mysterious and violent character in London's park

definitions.meaning: the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novel
a large royal park in central London

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is Stevenson's sinister brute, and Hyde Park is a famous royal park in London.

clue.text: Ultra-conservative Elmer, perhaps useless, departs within two years

parts.note: Elmer Fudd is the cartoon hunter who chases Bugs Bunny

indicators.note: within places the useless and departs pieces inside the two years
two calls for the abbreviation for year to be written twice

parts.note: Y is the standard abbreviation for year
a dud is something useless
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A stuffy man named Elmer, hopeless, leaves within two years.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned, fussy person who resists change is ultra-conservative, a stick-in-the-mud.
